design_scope.status: design proposals only; not implementation authorization

slices.title: Typed triple identity and canonical signed records
slices.goal: Define general typed-byte triple terms, object references, exact content/payload/envelope identity profiles, canonical signed body, and storage adapter seam without requiring RDF semantics.
slices.enables: Every later graph/query/attribute surface can share deterministic signed semantics and existing stores can materialize indexes without changing signed truth.

follow_up.owner: Atlas content identity owner to be assigned by summit; not an implementation assumption in #9125
follow_up.gap: Baseline found no checked-in Atlas production content_hash producer; define source bytes, exact profile/algorithm, producer location and compatibility vectors before new producers depend on it. Preserve separate Iroh BLAKE3, event BLAKE3, artifact SHA-256 and legacy JSON/Ed25519 profiles.
follow_up.docs_code_mismatch: Track the signed-artifact documentation/preimage mismatch against serde_json::to_vec(SignedBody); never silently change or re-sign legacy bytes.

tests.oracle: Independent reference codec recomputes exact canonical Body, PayloadId, EnvelopeId and signature preimages; arbitrary typed bytes round-trip, IDs exclude self-reference, malformed/noncanonical inputs reject, and profile-distinct hashes never coerce.

slices.title: Rebuildable ordered triple indexes and streaming scans
slices.goal: Add an initial redb materialization with rebuildable SPO/POS/OSP indexes and bounded continuation scans; keep index bytes outside signed authority.
slices.enables: Bounded graph patterns and pages can execute without loading the full logical graph.

tests.oracle: Pure in-memory typed-set matcher; rebuild and all indexed leading-component scans return exactly the same assertion IDs at a fixed frontier after shuffled ingestion, missing index and corruption.

slices.title: Bounded read-only triple-pattern API and cursors
slices.goal: Expose conjunctive typed triple patterns with stable ordering, opaque snapshot cursor, mandatory page limit, server-side authorization and a finite operator-validated budget profile.
slices.enables: Attributes, social projections and any later visualization share one authorized graph read path.

tests.oracle: Pure pattern matcher over canonical fixtures; cursor pages concatenate exactly to a fixed-frontier ordered result without duplicates/omissions; unauthorized and budget-exceeded queries cannot claim complete results.

slices.title: Bounded graph viewer over query pages
slices.goal: Build an optional native-shell graph viewer using the same authorized paged query API; visibly represent cycles, provenance, missing refs and incomplete/truncated pages.
slices.enables: Humans can inspect graph neighborhoods without a separate graph store or false-complete whole-graph picture.
slices.trigger: Only when a human-facing graph inspection surface is prioritized; not required for V2 graph query conformance.

tests.oracle: Golden graph fixture asserts visible cycle reference, provenance label, missing-reference state and truncation affordance; rendered node/edge set equals authorized QueryPage rows.

slices.title: Query-language adapter decision and conformance profile
slices.goal: Decide whether a named query language is justified by concrete RDF/interoperability use, and define its exact bounded feature profile over the typed API.
slices.enables: A selected language remains a semantics-preserving adapter rather than a second query engine or implicit RDF claim.

owned_files.status: new only if a language is selected

slices.trigger: Contingent on an explicit RDF or external-language interoperability requirement; no parser ships by default.

tests.oracle: If selected, supported W3C fixtures and typed-API equivalence fixtures agree; unsupported updates, paths or unbounded constructs are rejected, never silently approximated.

slices.title: Signed user-attribute definitions and policy
slices.goal: Define signed attribute objects, scope, and explicit closed/open/moderated submission policy distinct from Atlas and content-location metadata.
slices.enables: A validated per-attribute policy exists before append admission and social surfaces depend on it.

tests.oracle: Independent schema/policy model; canonical definitions round-trip; malformed scope, unauthorized policy edits and cross-tenant refs reject.

slices.title: Append submission, mandatory pending gate, and atomic approval
slices.goal: Verify signed submissions before pending/admission; force every non-group submitter to Pending even on open attributes; permit direct accept only for eligible in-group submitters; approve by CAS after current policy recheck.
slices.enables: A server-authoritative accepted list with immutable order and a safe moderation gate is available to consumers.

tests.oracle: MBT reference model proves invalid signature never enters pending/accepted; non-group submissions stay pending when open; approval CAS rechecks membership, policy and revocation; same idempotency key/different payload conflicts; accepted order never rewrites; epoch transition prevents sequence wrap.

slices.title: Nested topic/comment objects and bounded feed projections
slices.goal: Define immutable topic/comment/reaction/feed references and iterative, bounded nested traversal without prescribing one app’s ranking.
slices.enables: Feeds, profiles and bulletin-board projections can compose over signed graph objects.

tests.oracle: Reference iterative traversal model; cyclic/nested fixture obeys selected finite deployment profile and surfaces backrefs/truncation; returned relations match exact authorized graph set.

slices.title: Scoped social-feed freshness cursor and delta pages
slices.goal: Add opaque cursor bound to tenant, query, projection generation, epoch/sequence, frontier and expiry; return unchanged only when retained scoped history proves no newer visible data.
slices.enables: Clients check latest/since/before without rescanning a whole forum and never mistake cursor expiry for no changes.

tests.oracle: Reference ordered projection-log model; unchanged iff no later visible event exists at cursor scope; reset, retention gap, stale MAC, query/tenant replay and invalidation return typed expired/mismatch states.

slices.title: Canonical v1-succeeds-v2 version DAG and branch projection
slices.goal: Store explicit `(predecessor_v1, succeeds, successor_v2)` edges, validate same logical object and acyclic lineage, adapt equivalent legacy Supersede records without rewriting, and preserve competing heads.
slices.enables: Immutable edits and explicit branch-aware current-version views are available.

tests.oracle: Pure DAG model asserts stored edge direction v1→v2; cycles reject when ancestry complete, incomplete lineage stays pending, and all valid concurrent heads remain observable.

slices.title: Default ancestor-comment carry with origin marker
slices.goal: Carry comments from version ancestry into the default newer-version view, with old-version marker and transitive origin, while preserving original target and branch separation.
slices.enables: Readers see historical discussion on v2 without implying comments addressed changed content.

tests.oracle: Model projection includes each eligible ancestor comment once with immutable original target/origin and old marker; access/moderation/deletion filters still apply and sibling branches do not leak.

slices.title: Deletion requests, moderation queue and local true-delete states
slices.goal: Represent author/group deletion request, review queue, projection hide and server-policy true-delete as distinct signed states and bounded batch transitions.
slices.enables: A server can moderate/withhold locally without rewriting signed object identity or claiming global deletion.

tests.oracle: MBT model distinguishes request/queue/hide/physical-delete; batch retries are idempotent, evidence retention policy is honored, and one replica's local action does not mutate another replica's signed set.

slices.title: Fenced reference-aware graph garbage collection
slices.goal: Implement deletion-generation tombstone/fencing and CAS against reference-index generation/retention before physical removal; consume #9137 and #9084 ref-vs-copy semantics before enabling shared-object deletion.
slices.enables: GC cannot race a fresh reference or resurrect/delete content across an old worker fence.
slices.trigger: Physical GC remains disabled until #9137 and #9084 define compatible refcount/copy/retention generations and the adapter supports fenced atomic compare-and-delete.

tests.oracle: Concurrent model interleaves new reference, stale GC worker, restart and policy retention; no referenced/retained object is removed and older fence cannot delete after generation advance.

slices.title: Immutable signer-bound space address and local petnames
slices.goal: Define canonical typed `[null, public-key-bytes]` binding verification offline; keep binding immutable and petnames local; specify successor proof at original address or explicit signed redirect to new address.
slices.enables: Clients can attribute a space binding to a key without trusting the serving server or overwriting the old key address.

tests.oracle: Independent signature verifier accepts exact canonical binding offline; wrong key/position/version fail; transfer cannot mutate original address binding; new-address redirect requires old-key proof; petname cannot alter ID or authorization.

slices.title: Bounded delegation chains and two-key control transfer
slices.goal: Implement scope-attenuating delegation and distinct accepted transfer with replay protection, expiry, cycle rejection, finite chain budget, latest-frontier revocation and stale-frontier write denial.
slices.enables: A client/server can authorize a delegated location write without conflating a continuing grant with replacement ownership.

tests.oracle: Pure authority-chain model; no grant exceeds parent scope; duplicate nonce/replay, cycles, expired links, old fences and over-depth chains fail closed; transfer requires both keys over identical transfer/scope/challenge/domain/expiry bytes.

slices.title: Mutual cross-signed key-link challenge
slices.goal: Represent mutual key-link claims over identical challenge bytes binding pair, purpose/domain, scope, nonce and expiry; keep link status separate from identity/account equivalence and authority.
slices.enables: Clients can show verified mutual key claims without silently merging identity or privileges.

tests.oracle: Both signatures verify over same challenge bytes; unrelated, unilateral, mismatched-scope/nonce/domain/expiry or revoked statements remain pending/invalid; identity resolver never merges accounts or authorization from link alone.
